todaysEvents.delta: Reuters/Kpler said commodity-vessel transits fell to nine on Sep 24 from 14 on Sep 23, against an 18-vessel 10-day average. Crude exports were 33.7 million barrels week-to-date across 19 tankers, including 17 VLCCs.

Reuters said Saudi crude exports via Hormuz were on track for 3.6 million bpd in September versus 0.9 million bpd in August. Gulf of Oman ship-to-ship transfers reached capacity; a Middle East-to-China VLCC charter cost $1.27 million/day on Sep 21.

todaysEvents.summary: Oil settles lower on truce hopes
todaysEvents.delta: Reuters said Brent settled at $104.32/bbl on Sep 25, down 2.1%, after truce hopes. The report also noted six Houthi missiles intercepted toward Taif/Yanbu and that Yanbu tanker loadings had yet to resume; no signed Hormuz reopening is verified.

scenarios.label: Base
scenarios.description: Signed, monitored reopening and verified shipping normalisation are still required. Reuters said Yanbu tanker loadings had yet to resume; no signed commercial Hormuz reopening is verified.

scenarios.label: Stress
scenarios.description: Talks continue without an agreed reopening; Sep 24 commodity-vessel transits were nine against an 18-vessel 10-day average, while Saudi exports depend on congested Hormuz and full ship-to-ship capacity.

scenarios.label: Tail
scenarios.description: Conditional talks fail or Iran-linked and Houthi attacks widen, keeping Hormuz traffic selective and Gulf transfers congested; Qatar replacement LNG, route-normalised freight and war-risk costs remain unverified.
